The TEN welcome the HOU as underdogs of 3.5, with the total set at 43.5 — a market that implies a HOU 24–20 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 33% of its snaps with HOU in front, 42% within one score, and 25% with HOU chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

A modest edge to HOU. They should lead more often than not, tilting them slightly toward the run late, while TEN leans a touch more pass-heavy to stay in it — but the effect is gentle; this isn't a script that dramatically reshapes anyone's usage.

The Key Matchups

Tough sledding for Tony Pollard — HOU are stingy against the run (100 yds/game, well below the ~120 norm); lean under on his rushing line.

Sneaky value on Xavier Hutchinson (WR2) — TEN leak 44 yds/game to the WR2 role, above the ~36 norm.

Touchdown Board

Nico Collins carries TD equity — TEN surrender 0.53 WR1 receiving scores a game.

Game Script, Pace & Environment

A modest lean to HOU — they should lead more often than not, nudging them toward the run late and giving Woody Marks a gentle game-script tailwind.

HOU — a balanced offense

HOU are a balanced offense — their run/pass split by game state tracks the league closely (43% pass when leading vs 44% average), so their players' usage is driven more by role than by any strong situational lean.

Woody Marks (13 carries, 47 yards projected) gets a mild game-script tailwind as a favorite, though HOU's willingness to keep throwing when ahead caps how much the lead converts into extra carries.

Nico Collins projects for 6 targets and 58 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Dalton Schultz (TE, 4 targets, 29 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

TEN — a run-heavy offense

TEN are one of the league's more run-committed offenses: on early downs while leading, they pass just 38% of the time, against a league average of 44% — a genuine clock-bleeding identity, not noise (it holds after shrinking their sample toward the league).

Game script works against the run here — TEN project to trail and throw, which squeezes Tony Pollard's rushing projection (14 carries, 64 yards) but raises his value as a receiver; trailing teams check the ball down, and his target share ticks up as the game gets away from them.

Wan'Dale Robinson is the one to target from a volume standpoint: as underdogs throwing to keep pace, TEN funnel work to their top receiver — 8 targets for 49 yards projected, with genuine upside if they fall behind early and the game turns one-dimensional.

Underneath, Gunnar Helm (TE, 3 targets, 23 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

What to watch

The single biggest swing factor is availability — use the injury tool in the sidebar to mark anyone out; a starter's absence doesn't just remove his line, it redistributes his targets and carries to specific teammates, and the report and projections rebuild around it. Beyond that: if this game breaks toward the projected 4-point margin, the garbage-time backups (the ◆-flagged rows below) are where soft lines and real edge tend to appear — those depth players get fed in blowouts, and the market is slowest to price them.

This preview and the projections below regenerate through the week as injuries, weather and line moves update the inputs.
